Aggregate a panel to a coarser time unit

Source: R/aggregate_panel.R
aggregate_panel.Rd

Collapses a country-day, country-month, or country-quarter panel to a coarser unit ("month", "quarter", or "year"), for example to check monthly results against annual ones or to combine sources at different units.

Columns are combined by these default rules:

  • Conflict counts and totals (columns from add_conflict() such as *_n_events, *_total, n_campaigns, and NAVCO 3.0 fatalities and injuries): summed.

  • Other numeric conflict columns, including onset and incidence indicators and maxima: maximum. Counts of distinct units (*_n_active, arc_n_orgs) also take the maximum, a lower bound: the same episode or organization can appear in several periods, so their sum would double-count.

  • Conflict means and shares (*_mean_*, *_share_*): mean of the period values. This is not the mean over the underlying events.

  • Character conflict columns: the distinct values, joined by "; ".

  • All other columns (country names, annual data such as GDP, leaders): the value in the last period, i.e. at the end of the new period.

Sums and maxima of all-NA values are NA. Lags (*_l) and spell counters (*_spell) are dropped: recompute them on the aggregated panel with add_lag() and add_spell_duration().

Usage

aggregate_panel(
  panel,
  to = c("year", "quarter", "month"),
  sum = NULL,
  max = NULL,
  mean = NULL,
  last = NULL
)

Arguments

panel

A panel from build_states_panel() with unit = "day", "month", or "quarter", with any added data.

to

Target unit: "year" (default), "quarter", or "month". Must be coarser than the panel's unit.

sum, max, mean, last

Optional character vectors of column names that override the default rule for those columns.

Value

A panel at the unit to, with one row per country and period and the same columns as panel except the finer time keys, date, lags, and spell counters.

Examples

monthly <- build_states_panel(2010, 2012, coding_system = "cow", unit = "month") |>
  add_gdp() |>
  add_conflict("mmad", fill_zero = TRUE)

yearly <- aggregate_panel(monthly, to = "year")
#> Aggregated country-month to country-year. Summed: mmad_n_events, mmad_n_anti_gov, mmad_numreports_total. Mean of period values: mmad_mean_participants. Maximum: 4 other conflict column(s). Other columns take the value of the last month.
yearly[yearly$cow == 651, c("year", "gdp_pcap", "mmad_onset", "mmad_n_events")]
#>     year gdp_pcap mmad_onset mmad_n_events
#> 378 2010 13128.99          1            37
#> 379 2011 13082.43          1           233
#> 380 2012 13076.81          1            69
